title: Angular Advantages and Limitations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Angular Advantages and Limitations”?
options: Angular Advantages and Limitations means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Angular Advantages and Limitations removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Angular Advantages and Limitations should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Angular Advantages and Limitations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Angular Advantages and Limitations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Angular Advantages and Limitations is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Framework conventions and built-in features” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Framework conventions and built-in features” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Framework conventions and built-in features” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Framework conventions and built-in features” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Framework conventions and built-in features” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Framework conventions and built-in features” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Framework conventions and built-in features” under Angular Advantages and Limitations. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Angular Advantages and Limitations”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
